title: Galois Orbits and Descent of Simple Finite-Group Modules

items.title: Semilinear Galois actions, twists, and split central idempotents
items.statement: Let E/F be finite Galois with group Γ and A a finite-dimensional unital F-algebra. Set B=E⊗_F A and σ_B(e⊗a)=σ(e)⊗a. A semilinear action on an E-space W consists of additive maps T_σ with T_σ(ew)=σ(e)T_σ(w), T_1=id, T_σT_τ=T_{στ}; compatibility with B means T_σ(bw)=σ_B(b)T_σ(w). For a B-module W define {}^σW on its underlying additive group by b⋆w=σ_B^{-1}(b)w, including the changed E-scalar action. Thus {}^σ({}^τW)={}^(στ)W. In a transported E-basis its matrices for a∈A are σ(ρ(a)). A central idempotent is c∈Z(B) with c²=c; it is primitive if c≠0 and cannot be written as a sum of two nonzero orthogonal central idempotents. A split semisimple E-algebra means a finite product of full matrix E-algebras (empty product allowed for the zero algebra). For a left A-module S, E⊗_F S carries the left B-action (e⊗a)(f⊗s)=ef⊗as; balancing over the central field F makes this well-defined. Extension of scalars here is first along the commutative field map F→E, followed by this explicit algebra action; it does not apply the published commutative-ring definition to A→B. The stabilizer (decomposition group) of a simple-module class is Γ_W={σ∈Γ : {}^σW≅W}.

references.title: Weizhe Zheng, Lectures on Algebra (10 January 2025)

items.title: Galois fixed points recover finite-dimensional scalar extensions
items.statement: For a finite Galois E/F and a finite-dimensional semilinear Γ-space W, multiplication E⊗_F W^Γ→W is an E-linear isomorphism. If W is an E-algebra and Γ acts by semilinear algebra automorphisms, it is an algebra isomorphism. In particular, for the canonical action on E⊗_F V one has (E⊗_F V)^Γ=1⊗V, and E⊗_F(E⊗_F V)^Γ≅E⊗_F V; this respects algebra multiplication when V is an F-algebra. The map V→E⊗_F V, v↦1⊗v, is injective.

references.title: Weizhe Zheng, Lectures on Algebra (10 January 2025)

items.proof_plan: Choose an F-basis a_i of E and its trace-dual basis b_i. Dedekind independence makes the square embeddings matrix invertible. From Tr(a_i b_j)=δ_ij derive Σ_i a_i σ(b_i)=δ_{σ,1}. Then P_i(w)=Σ_σ σ(b_i)T_σ(w) is invariant, and Σ_i a_i P_i(w)=w. This proves surjectivity without division by |Γ|. For injectivity use a minimal E-linear relation among F-independent invariant vectors, normalize one coefficient to 1, subtract its σ-transform and use E^Γ=F. In the canonical tensor case coefficient uniqueness in an F-basis of V proves the fixed-space equality. Multiplication and units are preserved on elementary tensors; no general algebraic-geometric descent theorem is used.

items.title: Orbit sums of primitive split central idempotents descend
items.statement: Assume B=E⊗_F A is split semisimple. Its primitive central idempotents are exactly the coordinate identities in any split matrix decomposition. They correspond bijectively to simple B-module isomorphism classes by support. The semilinear Γ-action permutes them, compatibly with the twist convention: c supports W if and only if σ_B(c) supports {}^σW. For each orbit O, c_O=Σ_{c∈O}c equals 1⊗e_O for a unique nonzero central idempotent e_O∈A. Distinct e_O are orthogonal and their sum is 1.

references.title: Weizhe Zheng, Lectures on Algebra (10 January 2025)
references.locator: §3.2 Theorem 3.2.1 and §3.8 Theorem 3.8.1; central-idempotent argument reconstructed locally

items.proof_plan: The center of each M_n(E) is E, whose only idempotents are 0 and 1. This proves the coordinate-idempotent description, including that every central idempotent is a sum of a unique subset. Apply the published column-module classification for support. A semilinear algebra automorphism preserves centrality, orthogonality and primitivity. The twist formula gives σ_B(c)⋆w=cw. Orbit sums are invariant; the previous lemma descends them to A. Injectivity of A→E⊗A reflects idempotence, centrality (test commutators with 1⊗a), nonzeroness and orthogonality.

items.title: Descended orbit idempotents are primitive and their blocks have one simple type
items.statement: Let A be a finite-dimensional semisimple F-algebra and B=E⊗_F A split semisimple, with E/F finite Galois. The e_O of the orbit-sum lemma are precisely the primitive central idempotents of A. Each block Ae_O is simple Artinian and has exactly one simple left-module isomorphism class. If Ae_O≅M_n(D) and S=D^n, then D≅End_A(S)^op.

references.title: Weizhe Zheng, Lectures on Algebra (10 January 2025)
references.locator: §3.2 Theorem 3.2.1, Remark 3.2.3; §3.3 Lemma 3.3.2 and Warning 3.3.3(1), pp.117–118; §3.8 Theorem 3.8.1

items.proof_plan: If e_O=f+g is a nontrivial orthogonal central splitting over F, then 1⊗f and 1⊗g split O into nonempty disjoint Γ-stable subsets, impossible for one orbit. Since the e_O sum to 1, any primitive central idempotent e has exactly one nonzero product ee_O and equals it, hence equals e_O. To justify the block consequence, use Wedderburn–Artin. In M_n(D), comparison with matrix units shows a central element is dI with d∈Z(D); its central idempotents are 0 and I because D is a division ring. Every nonzero two-sided ideal in M_n(D) contains all matrix units by multiplying a nonzero entry on both sides and inverting that entry. Thus the primitive factors are simple Artinian. The published simple-module classification gives one column-module type. Retain opposite-ring orientation D≅End_A(S)^op.

items.title: Galois orbits classify simple modules after splitting base change
items.statement: In ZFC, let A be a finite-dimensional semisimple unital F-algebra and E/F a finite Galois extension such that E⊗_F A is split semisimple. There is a canonical bijection between simple left A-module isomorphism classes and Γ-orbits O of simple left (E⊗_F A)-module isomorphism classes. If S corresponds to O, then E⊗_F S≅⊕_[W]∈O W^{⊕m_S} for a uniquely determined positive integer m_S. Distinct simple A-modules have disjoint constituent sets; every simple extended module occurs. This includes A=0 with empty sets. For a finite group G and char F=0, apply this to A=F[G] and any finite Galois E/F which is a splitting field for G. Thus the statement concerns irreducible representations over arbitrary characteristic-zero F, without assuming F algebraically closed or the common multiplicity equal to one.

references.title: Weizhe Zheng, Lectures on Algebra (10 January 2025)
references.locator: Proposition 4.3.2, pp.145–146 (block/scalar-extension multiplicities); Theorem 3.8.1, pp.132–133; Theorem 4.1.6, p.139 (averaging proof, expanded here in finite dimension)

items.proof_plan: Use orbit idempotents to assign to O the unique simple Ae_O-module S. Wedderburn–Artin gives Ae_O≅S^{⊕n} as a left A-module for some n>0. Extending scalars gives Bc_O≅(E⊗S)^{⊕n}. The split regular block is a direct sum of its column modules, so the constituent support of E⊗S is exactly O, and E⊗S is semisimple as a direct summand of that finite regular block (explicitly, for M over M_d(E), write M=⊕_j E_jj M, choose an E-basis v_t of E_11 M and map the standard column basis vector in position j of copy t to E_j1 v_t; these images give a module isomorphism (E^d)^{⊕dim E_11 M}≅M; do this in each factor). Canonical semilinear maps on E⊗S identify its twist with itself. Uniqueness of finite semisimple multiplicities, or dimensions of the matrix-unit subspaces, gives equal positive multiplicity throughout O. This proves surjectivity, injectivity and uniqueness. For the finite-group specialization, prove semisimplicity over each k=F,E locally instead of consuming the unrepaired published Maschke chain. For a finite-dimensional k[G]-module V and submodule U, use thm-dimension-of-a-linear-subspace clause 3 to choose a finite basis of U extended to V; retaining the U coordinates defines a linear projection P onto U. The characteristic lemma and def-field make |G|·1_k invertible (G contains its identity, so |G|>0). Set Q=|G|^(-1)Σ_g gPg^(-1), with sums in the additive commutative monoid of endomorphisms. Finite distributivity follows by strong induction and the field/module axioms; reindexing g↦hg shows hQh^(-1)=Q. Each summand maps into U and fixes U, so Q(V)⊆U and Q|U=id. Therefore V=U⊕ker Q by v=Qv+(v-Qv), and ker Q is a submodule. Strong induction on dim_k V gives a finite direct sum of simple submodules: the zero case is empty, a nonzero simple V is done, otherwise split any nonzero proper submodule U; U and ker Q are proper subspaces and have strictly smaller dimensions by thm-dimension-of-a-linear-subspace clause 2. Apply this to the finite regular module k[G], whose group basis and module dictionary are supplied by thm-group-actions-and-group-ring-modules-correspond and its group-ring prerequisite. The semisimple-module and semisimple-ring definitions now give semisimplicity. Identify E⊗FG≅EG on the group basis. The given splitting-field endomorphism condition and Wedderburn–Artin force each division factor to be E, with the opposite ring accounted for. No existence assertion for a finite Galois splitting field is silently imported from the recorded Brauer criterion.

title: Galois Orbits and Descent of Simple Finite-Group Modules: Examples

items.title: Descent of the two nontrivial characters of C₃
items.statement: For F=Q, E=Q(ζ) with ζ²+ζ+1=0, and C₃=⟨g:g³=1⟩, multiplication by ζ on S=Q(ζ) is represented in the basis (1,ζ) by [[0,-1],[1,-1]]. This rational module is simple and its scalar extension is the sum of the two distinct one-dimensional modules g↦ζ and g↦ζ², each with multiplicity one. Their orbit has size two; the rational trace is 2 at 1 and -1 at g,g².

references.title: Weizhe Zheng, Lectures on Algebra (10 January 2025)
references.locator: Theorem 3.8.1, Example 3.8.2 and Proposition 4.3.2, specialized to the quadratic cyclotomic field

items.proof_plan: Check the matrix cube and its irreducible minimal polynomial over Q (the polynomial has no rational root). Over E its two distinct eigenvalues give two eigenlines. Conjugation exchanges these eigenlines. Explicitly e=(2-g-g²)/3 is the nontrivial rational central idempotent, and evaluation g↦ζ identifies Q[C₃]e with Q(ζ); check e²=e, its dimension two, and the evaluation kernel. E/Q is finite Galois because its two roots ζ,ζ² lie in E. Compute traces directly.

items.title: The rational simple quaternion block
items.statement: Use the published quaternion group Q₈, writing its generators as u,v, so Q₈={±1,±u,±v,±uv}, u²=v²=-1 and vu=-uv; put z=-1 as a group element. The central idempotent e=(1-z)/2 in Q[Q₈] cuts out the division algebra D=Q[Q₈]e≅(-1,-1)_Q of dimension four. Its unique simple module is D. For E=Q(i), E⊗_Q D≅M₂(E), and E⊗_Q D is two copies of the degree-two simple module W. W has trace values 2,-2,0,0,0 on the conjugacy classes 1,z,{±u},{±v},{±uv}; its Galois orbit is a singleton, with descent multiplicity two.

references.title: Weizhe Zheng, Lectures on Algebra (10 January 2025)
references.locator: Example 3.7.4(3), p.125 (norm calculation adapted to Q); Proposition 4.3.2

references.title: Gábor Wiese, Galois Representations
references.locator: Remark 2.4.2(ii), p.34; Exercise 14, p.70 (real quaternion example adapted to Q and Q(i))

items.proof_plan: Use the basis e,ue,ve,uve and compute quaternion multiplication. Conjugation gives q q̄=a²+b²+c²+d², nonzero for nonzero rational q, so D is division. Embed D into M₂(E) by u↦diag(i,-i), v↦[[0,1],[-1,0]]; the images of 1,u,v,uv form an E-basis and prove the splitting isomorphism. Column ideals decompose the left regular module as W⊕W. The other rational block (1-e)Q[Q₈] identifies with Q[C₂×C₂]; its four evaluation homomorphisms to Q give Q⁴ by the invertible sign matrix. Hence E splits the entire group algebra, as required to apply the theorem. Conjugation on E sends u to -u and fixes v, and conjugation by the displayed v matrix intertwines the two representations. Compute all traces explicitly.

items.title: A Galois-stable character need not descend with multiplicity one
items.statement: The rational-valued degree-two character of Q₈ from the preceding example is fixed by Gal(Q(i)/Q), yet no two-dimensional Q-representation affords it. Its least positive rational realization multiplicity is two (the Schur multiplicity obstruction). Thus Galois stability alone does not imply descent of the individual simple module.

references.title: Weizhe Zheng, Lectures on Algebra (10 January 2025)
references.locator: Example 3.7.4(3) and Proposition 4.3.2 (explicit rational matrix obstruction computed locally)

items.proof_plan: If rational matrices U,V afforded this character, z would act as -I: z²=I and trace -2 imply both eigenvalues are -1 in characteristic zero. Hence U²=V²=-I and UV=-VU. A rational basis puts U=[[0,-1],[1,0]]; solving UV=-VU gives V=[[a,b],[b,-a]], so V²=(a²+b²)I≠-I over Q. This proves nonexistence without any later Schur-index theorem. The dimension-four rational module in the preceding example realizes two copies, proving the least positive multiplicity is exactly two. Do not cite the later canonical Schur-index definition as a dependency; explain that later terminology names this computed multiplicity.
